executiveSummary: GM0589 passes the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract. Its CBS/PDOK 2025 identity, 10,355-person municipality control, 18 neighbourhoods in four districts, four BAG places and ten BRT settlements are coherent; published neighbourhood rows sum exactly to the municipal population control. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Oudewater's relevant water system is the Gekanaliseerde Hollandsche IJssel (GHIJ), regional kades, polders, local drainage, sewer and groundwater, with active 2026–2027 dike work. A bounded LIWO query returns no primary candidate and six regional candidates, four contained by the generalized municipality boundary. Yet the named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel river preset reports exactly 1.244929 m from T+12 through T+72, 3,912 affected residents at T+24 and seven service values unchanged through T+72 without selecting a GHIJ case, water level, regional defence/structure state, connected footprint, arrival or recession. Direct open-coast water is correctly zero and should remain suppressed only in that narrow source scope. Pluvial reports 0.325143 m and Drainage availability 0.588381 at T+24 without the municipality's climate-adaptation, sewer, measured groundwater, AHN, pump, sluice or receiving-water state, then clears water and effects by an exact T+72 recovery. Storm, pluvial, river, heat, winter, cyber and compound reuse the same resident-heavy top-five neighbourhood order. This ignores Tappersheul's 120 residents alongside 165 businesses and 187 non-residential buildings and event/tourist populations in the historic centre. Mobility and supply use only two N228 logical edges representing one physical corridor; no A12 feeder-chain state, local bridge/dike-road restriction, rail alternative or destination-specific external care is routed. Public context contains 171 partial water/wastewater objects, one Stedin planning sample with null existing/required values, eighteen antenna sites and six education locations; no internal RIVM acute-care respondent or Waterinfo observation/forecast exists. VRU's 2025 Oudewater 72-hour power-outage exercise proves the importance of communications, payments, refrigeration, lighting and cross-sector coordination, but does not prove household, care, school or business readiness. Unknown, NoData, candidate catalogues, plans, registers and exercises must never become zero, safe, open or operational.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0589 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, settlement and safety-region context
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated snapshots retrieved 31 August–2 September 2026
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0589 as Oudewater in Utrecht and safety region Utrecht and report 10,355 residents, density 266/km², 23.1% aged 65 or older and 1,493 one-person households; the generated centre [4.862637954708087,52.02827092814908] lies inside the 2025 boundary.

Eighteen neighbourhood rows in four districts sum exactly to 10,355 residents, 4,490 households and 2,390 independently rounded age-65-plus residents. Allocation reconciles to the municipal control without rewriting source rows.

BAG supplies Hekendorp, Oudewater, Papekop and Snelrewaard. BRT supplies ten source-labelled settlements: five buurtschappen, one deelkern and four woonkernen. No BAG place centre falls outside the generalized boundary.

All 36 CBS fields are exposed. District heating and public charging are null in all 18 rows; cars per household is null in six and several housing/benefit fields in three. Null/suppression remains NoData. CBS/PDOK is CC BY 4.0 and BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Current GHIJ-Noord and Willeskop regional-dike and bank-improvement programmes
evidenceSources.edition: Current project pages and 4 May 2026 execution notice inspected 3 September 2026; expected completion end 2027
supports: HDSR is renewing eight kilometres of kade on the north side of the GHIJ between Montfoort and Hekendorp; execution began in July 2026 and is expected to finish at the end of 2027.

The 4 May 2026 notice at https://www.hdsr.nl/%40229272/uitvoering-dijkverbetering/ says strengthened waterside dikes will replace some double-kade arrangements and become the official regional water barrier, with river widening at Bokkenkade and a side channel at Waardsedijk.

HDSR reports the six-kilometre south-side Willeskop improvement between Montfoort and Oudewater almost complete at https://www.hdsr.nl/buurt/gekanaliseerde/dijken/dijk-oeververbetering-willeskop-deel-2/dijk-oeververbetering-willeskop-bijna/ and Hekendorp bank maintenance complete in April 2026.

Programme scope and future-standard work establish a regional-water pathway and changing construction geometry, not an event-time failure, breach, closure or consequence forecast. No blanket machine-reuse licence or live component-state feed was identified on the pages.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — LIWO 2025.1.6 regional candidate catalogue and absent local Waterinfo coverage
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO application 2025.1.6; bounded WFS and Waterinfo deployment snapshots queried 3 September 2026
supports: The bounded query returns zero primary and six regional candidates. Point-in-polygon against the generated generalized boundary contains four: HIJ_0005 Oudewater-oost, HIJ_0006 Oudewater-west, HIJ_0007 Hekendorp and HIJ_0008 Polder Lange Weide.

Dijkring15 and HIJ_0009 Polder Stein-oost lie in the query envelope but outside the generalized boundary. Administrative containment and candidate naming still require HDSR authority association rather than automatic selection.
Candidate points, open-water/dike-ring ids and frequency flags are scenario-selection metadata, not active failures, forecasts, connected footprints, metre depths, arrival or safe-state evidence.

The generated Waterinfo snapshots assign no observation or forecast to GM0589. Missing station/horizon coverage remains NoData. Waterinfo is CC0/non-mission-critical; LIWO release/licence and authority approval must remain attached.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Oudewater / Hoogheemraadschap De Stichtse Rijnlanden
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Local climate-adaptation, sewer, groundwater and subsidence mechanisms
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal and HDSR public guidance inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipality identifies water nuisance, drought, heat stress and flooding as separate adaptation themes. It states intense short rain can exceed sewer capacity, leave water in streets/tunnels, enter buildings or impede emergency services.

The groundwater page at https://www.oudewater.nl/Wonen/Grondwater says the municipality measures groundwater through distributed monitoring wells; high groundwater can cause moisture and low groundwater can threaten wooden pile foundations. It distinguishes public-space and private responsibilities.

HDSR groundwater guidance at https://www.hdsr.nl/werk/grondwateroverlast/ warns that saturated ground follows heavy rain and that lowering groundwater in settlement-sensitive peat areas can cause subsidence and building damage.

Static guidance and monitoring availability are not a selected rainfall, sewer model, observation field, foundation condition, completed measure or event-time pump/receiving-water state. No machine API or blanket redistribution licence was identified.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Public water-chain and control-asset context
evidenceSources.edition: HWH deployment snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026; current HDSR pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Generated non-generalized containment assigns 171 HWH objects: two sewer pumps, twelve surface-water pumps, one wastewater treatment plant, two sluices and 154 weirs. HWH IMWA/DAMO is contributor-dependent/partial, weekly where supplied and CC BY-SA 4.0.

The register identifies Oudewater Noord and Zuid sewer pumps and RWZI Oudewater. HDSR says Oudewater wastewater is treated locally and discharged to the Hollandse IJssel; its current address list locates the plant at Goudsestraatweg 76.

Register status 'gerealiseerd', point type and capacity fields are static asset metadata, not proof of connected catchment, compatible capacity, live operation, backup power, staffing, inflow, effluent, control or restoration.
No complete current GWSW sewer topology, monitoring-well time series or event-time GHIJ/polder/pump/sluice state is consumed. Absence or partial contributor coverage remains Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — N228, scheduled transit, missing rail and external acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail snapshot and GTFS v9543 valid 30 August–12 December 2026; RIVM acute care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: The simulator has two logical edges, both the same physical N228 corridor: west to Krimpenerwaard (3.57 km) and east to Montfoort (0.10 km), each with 150 scenario units. No independent second road corridor is present.
No ProRail station is assigned. Eight scheduled-transit stops are present at J.J. Vierbergenweg, Lijnbaan, Molenwal, Papekop, Tappersheul, Tramweg, Willeskop Lekkerkerker and Willeskop Van Dam.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 is CC0 and assigns no respondent acute point inside GM0589. Approximate centre-distance sites are 24/7 Groene Hart Gouda 10.73 km, St. Antonius Nieuwegein 14.87 km and St. Antonius Utrecht 15.70 km; distance is not route time, ambulance state or acceptance.

NWB is CC0 and RIVM is CC0. Static route, station/stop and schedule geometry does not establish road/bridge operation, bus service, accessibility, passenger load, emergency priority, hospital acceptance or alternative access.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Historic-centre, tourism and Tappersheul dynamic-exposure context
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal project page inspected 3 September 2026; CBS neighbourhood statistics 2025; municipal Omgevingsvisie public evidence
supports: The municipality is actively expanding Tappersheul, with road and parking-ground preparation scheduled July–September 2026 and building preparation/construction from 2027.
CBS gives Tappersheul 120 residents, 165 businesses and 187 non-residential buildings. Resident population alone cannot represent workplace, construction, freight or sports-facility occupancy.

Municipal planning describes the historic centre as a mixed residential, retail and tourism area and identifies tourism/day visitors as economically material. The event calendar records time-specific licensed activities in the centre and elsewhere.

Plans, business/building counts and event listings do not provide incident-time persons, opening, freight, vulnerable occupancy, completed construction or emergency resource state. No blanket reuse licence for the municipal pages was identified.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Utrecht / Netbeheer Nederland / Stedin / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Oudewater 72-hour power-outage exercise and public utility/facility context
evidenceSources.edition: VRU story dated 13 October 2025; NBNL/RDI/DUO deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–2 September 2026
supports: VRU and Oudewater ran a 9 October 2025 walkthrough of a 72-hour large power outage with residents, care, education, retail, hospitality, housing, churches and emergency services. It identifies loss of communications, electronic payments, cooling and lighting and explored local roles and cooperation.

One NBNL sample maps to Stedin service area Waaiersluis. Existing/required withdrawal and injection values are null; zero queued MW/requests, TenneT classes and fourteen projects are planning context, not live load, outage, switching, reserve or proof of unconstrained capacity.

RDI assigns eighteen antenna sites—nine mobile, seven fixed-link and two amateur—and DUO six education locations—five primary and one other registered use. Register presence does not establish signal, occupancy, shelter role, backup power, water or restoration.

The exercise is preparedness/governance evidence, not proof every household or organization is ready. Exact NBNL reuse licence and blanket reuse rights for the VRU page were not identified; RDI/DUO source terms and validity must remain attached.

residualLimitations: This artifact audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a forecast, warning, evacuation instruction, hydraulic assessment, road/bridge decision, hospital status or operator restoration commitment.

CBS 2025 values are rounded/suppressed and residents exclude workers, construction crews, shoppers, tourists/event visitors, pupils, patients/staff, responders and displaced people; no timestamped dynamic occupancy is consumed.
Generalized polygons and centroids cannot resolve GHIJ hydraulic compartments, kades/structures, polders, sewers/groundwater, pumps/sluices, narrow bridges/roads, event sites or utility zones.
Four contained LIWO points are regional candidates, not breaches, observations or footprints. Query-envelope and generalized-boundary assignment requires HDSR authority review.
Current dike/bank work does not mean event-time failure. Construction phase, temporary access/geometry and component condition can change and remain Unknown without a valid feed.
Municipal climate/groundwater guidance establishes mechanisms and measurement availability, not a live rain event, groundwater field, sewer/pump state, foundation damage or local depth.
HWH coverage is partial/provider-dependent and register status/capacity is not connected live topology, compatible flow, backup, control or recovery.
Zero internal Waterinfo features is a coverage statement only; it does not imply normal GHIJ, groundwater, sewer, polder or asset conditions.
Two N228 logical edges share one physical corridor. NWB geometry is not live throughput; feeder chains, bridges/local roads, buses and alternatives need valid-time state without double counting.
Zero internal RIVM acute-care respondent points does not erase local care/demand. Centre distance is not route time, ambulance availability, acceptance, beds, staff, utilities or backup.
Tappersheul business/building totals, construction plans and municipal tourism/event context do not establish current occupants, freight, hazards, access or resource state.
One Stedin planning sample with null capacity values, eighteen antennas and six schools are planning/register context, not customer connectivity, load, signal, occupancy, shelter, backup or repair.
VRU's 72-hour power-outage walkthrough is preparedness/governance evidence, not proof of household supplies, communications, care continuity, generators, cash/payment alternatives or mutual aid.

Canonical wildfire's zero local flame is source-scope output, not proof that local vegetation or fire risk is absent; remote smoke and any future local ignition require distinct source/time/perimeter semantics.

Complete physical electricity, gas, drinking-water, wastewater, telecom, care, supply and emergency-resource topology/live state may be unavailable or security-sensitive and remains Unknown or explicitly synthetic.

Exact hazard, neighbourhood, affected-population, service-availability, recovery and person-hour values remain synthetic/derived screening until critical/high findings are corrected and authorities review the selected event; impacts beyond T+72 are outside scope.
